answer: An auditor observes two rings of verification. First, an account's work log must cite cedar-graded evidence, meaning signed logs from tools whose version and output hash are on record; hollow claims citing compute with no matching log fail and are logged as violations. Second, survivors are weighed by timber volume, meaning the ledger counts each verified log once and never credits duplicates. An operator fabricating accounts must forge tool signatures and unique log hashes per puppet, an expense repeated at scale, while a genuine account simply keeps accurate logs.
